newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Tenaga estimates raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Tenaga estimates raised.

text.p: Jupiter Securities said on Friday it has raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Tenaga Nasional Bhd following the utility's receipt of an 8.3 percent tariff increase effective on May 1.
In a report issued on Friday, Jupiter said it was increasing its 1997 net profit estimate to 1.22 billion ringgit from 996.3 million, or to 39.3 cents from 32.0 cents a share.
Its 1998 forecast was boosted to 1.99 billion ringgit from 1.23 billion, or to 64.2 cents from 39.5 cents a share.
The financial year for Tenaga, which is the dominant electricity generator in Malaysia, ends August 31.
In 1996, Tenaga reported net profit of 797.8 million ringgit or 25.9 cents a share.

The tariff hike raises average power prices to 23.5 cents per kilowatt hour. In addition, the government capped the cost of fuel used by Tenaga at 6.40 ringgit/MMBTU until the year 2000 from the current price of around 7.00 ringgit/MMBTU.
The rate hike is "within our expectation of an increase of up to 10 percent," the report from Jupiter said. It said it maintains its hold recommendation on the stock.
At 0213 GMT, Tenaga stock was at 11.70 ringgit, up 10 cents.
